title: A bug filed at the end of a task has been reproduced, not just read
goal: A task that finished last night filed a top priority bug saying the loop had stopped rebuilding the app you playtest with, so nobody was seeing their work. It was not true: the check that found it ran the wrong shell against the script, and the rebuild had in fact run and succeeded minutes earlier. A follow-up filed from reading rather than running costs a whole task cycle at the top of the queue, so the instructions a task runner works from should require the same standard for a bug it files as for the work it does. It unblocks the focus by protecting the top of the queue: a false top-priority bug takes the slot the focus feature would have had, which is exactly what happened on 2026-09-06.
notes: Design review 2026-09-06. Evidence: the-app-you-playtest-with-is-rebuilt-after-every, created 12:10 UTC, dropped in the same triage pass. Its notes said queue/bin/refresh-dev-app.sh was a bash syntax error; the file is #!/bin/zsh and zsh -n is clean, queue/loop.log holds 180 successful refreshes with the last at 05:10:36 the same morning, and go-loop.sh:125 already prints a line when a refresh fails, which the task also said was missing. queue/bin/runner-prompt.md has no rule about reproducing a bug before filing it (grep for reproduce finds nothing).
acceptance: The runner instructions say a follow-up that claims something is broken must carry the command that shows it broken, and its output
They say to run a script the way the machine runs it rather than reading it or checking it with another shell
They say what to do when it cannot be reproduced: file it as something to look into rather than as a bug, at normal priority
The daily triage pass is told to spot-check the evidence on any new top priority bug before it is allowed to run first

log.note: Triage 2026-09-07: kept at p3-low but moved to the front of it, since it is cheap and it guards the slot the focus work runs in.

Happened again on 2026-09-07: the-dev-app-is-rebuilt-after-every-task-again was filed p1 with the identical bash -n misreading of a zsh script, one day after the first one was dropped for the same reason. Two p1 runner slots spent on a non-bug. The zsh-only syntax that triggers the misread is gone as of this run, so this exact false positive cannot recur, but the underlying habit (filing from reading code, without running it) is what this task is for.

Adversarial review of the idea first. A prose rule alone gets skimmed, so it is placed at the exact moment of filing (directly under the addjson command a runner uses) and backed by a second gate in triage, which catches whatever slips past the first. Rejected for this task: making queue.mjs refuse a p1 with no evidence, because the schema has no way to tell a bug from a feature task and inventing a kind field is a separate change. Also scoped the rule deliberately: it binds bugs the loop files against itself, and exempts user reports, whose report is itself the evidence and which must stay p1.

Verified the facts before writing them down, since a doc that misstates its own example would be the same mistake. refresh-dev-app.sh is #!/bin/zsh; as of 324ab540 both bash -n and zsh -n are clean on it, so that exact false positive cannot recur and the rule is written about the habit, not the script. queue/loop.log holds 1127 refresh lines. grep for reproduc across queue/bin/*.md found nothing before this change.

Shipped: runner-prompt.md gains 'A bug you file must be reproduced, not just read' (show the command and its output, run a script with the interpreter on its shebang rather than reading it or checking it with another shell, look for evidence it already worked, and if it cannot be reproduced file it at p2-normal as an open question, never p0/p1). digest-prompt.md triage gains a spot-check bullet that reruns the evidence on every new p0/p1 bug and demotes any that has none. manager-prompt.md gains a one-line version, since the manager files bugs too. go-loop.sh cats all three at runtime (lines 103, 213, 263), so the next pass picks them up. Scripts/test.sh green, 4507 tests.

No audit written: this changes the instructions the loop works from, not the app, so there is nothing for the user to try. Left undone and worth a later look: nothing enforces this mechanically, so a runner determined to skip it still can.

runner-prompt.md now requires a bug to be reproduced before it is filed (command plus output in notes, run a script with the interpreter on its shebang, and file at p2-normal as an open question when it cannot be reproduced). digest-prompt.md triage spot-checks the evidence on every new p0/p1 bug and demotes any with none; manager-prompt.md carries the one line version.
